body.p: HelpDNA tells the story of Ernesto Behrens, an innocent man who has spent more than 26 years in the Florida Department of Corrections. We believe the evidence shows a wrongful conviction — and we are asking for the public's attention, voice, and support.

DNA forensic evidence is an invaluable tool for law enforcement — but it is most useful when it corroborates other evidence pointing to a suspect. When it does not, far more public oversight and accountability are warranted.

The fact that DNA alone can be used to obtain a conviction and support a life sentence should send chills down everyone's spine. The next Ernesto Behrens could be you, or someone you love. Be a voice.

pages.title: Ernesto's Story
pages.heroSub: An innocent man, more than 26 years imprisoned.

body.p: Ernesto Behrens has spent over 26 years in the Florida Department of Corrections for a crime we believe he did not commit. This site, begun by his friend Franziska Kaltenbach, documents his case and the long fight to prove his innocence.

Ernesto's conviction rested on DNA evidence that the defense maintains was mishandled and tampered with. The broader physical evidence did not point to him, and his account places him elsewhere at the time of the crime.

His journey through the courts — motions for DNA testing, appeals, petitions to innocence organizations and the state's conviction review unit — is chronicled in detail in the full archive of court documents and correspondence.

cta.heading: Go Deeper
cta.body: The complete archive of court documents, motions, and correspondence is published in full at helpdna.org.

meta.title: Ernesto's Story — HelpDNA
meta.description: The story of Ernesto Behrens, an innocent man imprisoned for over 26 years.

body.p: According to the case documented here, the prosecution's theory did not square with the physical evidence. Among the points raised in Ernesto's defense:

list: The suspect could not have been in two places at once.
The suspect had undergone surgery four days before the crime took place.
Fingerprints, palm prints, and shoe castings did not match.
The suspect did not match the victim's description of the assailant.
The defense's position is that the State tampered with the DNA evidence.

body.p: DNA technology is powerful — but it is handled by people, and people can err or act in bad faith. When a conviction rests on DNA alone, without corroboration, the public deserves rigorous oversight. Ernesto's case is a warning about what happens when that oversight fails.

Support the legal effort — contributions help fund the ongoing work to prove his innocence.
Share your own story if you or someone you know has faced wrongful conviction.
Help us reach attorneys willing to take the case pro bono.
